newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines raises power rates in all grids.
newsitem.headline: Philippines raises power rates in all grids.

text.p: The Philippines' National Power Corp raised power rates in all five grids on Wednesday by an average of 3.998 centavos per kilowatt-hour (kwh).
In a statement, the state-owned power firm said the northern island of Luzon will experience the biggest increase of 7.99 centavos per kwh.
The power firm said the increase in Luzon was brought about by the recent commercial operation of the 700-megawatt Pagbilao coal-fired power plant in the northern province of Quezon.
In central Philippines, Napocor raised rates in the Leyte-Samar grid by 7.72 centavos per kwh and in Cebu-Negros-Panay grid by 0.43 centavos. In Bohol, power rates will increase by 0.64 centavos.
In the southern island of Mindanao, Napocor raised rates by 3.21 centavos per kwh.
The adjustments in other grids was also brought about by increased cost of power bought from privately-operated power plants, Napocor said..
Napocor adjusts power rates monthly to reflect fluctuations in fuel cost and changes in the foreign exchange rates.
